derived: NVO turned 25.95% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 49.5% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: NVO paid 4,522mm DKK of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 0.54% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 29.59% to 29.04%. Restated at replacement capex: NVO spent 133,110mm DKK on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 19,625mm DKK of plant depreciation, 13.64% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 29.04% to 11.89%. Restated with selling costs: SG&A now carries NVO's filed selling or distribution costs, 20.81% of revenue this charge was absorbing, so it falls from 11.89% to nil. The filed lines alone now leave less than the cash the company made before interest and at replacement capex, and a charge below nil would credit the book with cash its own costs do not leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 41.40% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 50.32%, so the charge rebuilds at -8.92%. It was held at nil, but NVO books 6,529mm DKK of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0000353278-26-000012), 2.11% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -2.11%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVO's cash flow statement shows receivables up 20,296mm DKK, inventories up 25,235mm DKK, payables up 15,158mm DKK, a working capital build of 30,373mm DKK, 3.65% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -2.11% where the filed figures rebuild it at -8.92%, and stays there.

ARTEMIS registry record (NCT06118281, updated 2026-09-09): a subcutaneous loading dose as early as possible after the invasive procedure and within 36 hours of hospitalisation for STEMI or 48 hours for NSTEMI, then maintenance dosing, against placebo, with the primary endpoint followed for up to 25 months. Novo's FY2025 20-F (0000353278-26-000012) describes ziltivekimab as a monoclonal antibody in AMI among its Phase 3 projects
column12: Monthly maintenance dosing, so chronic. The case against: the label may follow the trial's roughly two-year treatment period. The discontinuation below gives a mean time on drug of about two years (1/0.505), so a fixed course and a chronic line land in about the same place

Converted at the ECB rate of 0.152643266 USD per DKK on 2026-09-23 (fetchers/fx_ecb.py, the rate the other Novo seeds use): DKK 30,855.04
column12: Judgement on the comparator: the self-injected antibody used for secondary prevention after a heart attack, and the largest by Medicare use. The 2024 basis was $4,266. Summed beneficiaries count a patient who changed container twice, so the figure leans low. Alternatives on the same 2025 basis: Praluent Pen $4,000.26 (84,102 beneficiaries) and Kevzara, an IL-6 antibody priced for rheumatology, $33,002.35. Novo would price for a mass cardiovascular population, not a rheumatology one. The case against: Repatha's own US exclusivity ends in 2029 (data/disclosed_loe.csv, from Amgen's 10-K), the year ziltivekimab would launch, and Lipfendra, the oral PCSK9 inhibitor, lists at $315 a month (azn_azd0780.csv), so the injectable anchor may be stale by then

column12: Wholly owned, with no co-development or profit share; the milestones are deal cash, not a revenue share. Corvidia licensed the antibody from AstraZeneca in 2016 (Fierce Biotech and BioSpace, 2016), and neither those reports nor Novo's filings state the licence's royalty terms; Novo books royalties in cost of goods sold only after approval and excludes them from its commitments note (20-F). A royalty to AstraZeneca cannot be ruled out, so 1.0 is a ceiling

Stating prevalence equal to incidence makes the engine read carryover 0 and no opening pool (forecast.patients_for_indication), so a patient not started at the index event leaves the pool; no explicit untreated_carryover_pct is written, because an explicit 0 keeps an opening pool and doubles year one

Of these, 605,000 are a first heart attack, and 200,000 happen to be people who have already had a heart attack.' The same page the AZD0780 seed cites
column12: First and recurrent heart attacks both count: ARTEMIS takes a prior heart attack as a qualifying risk criterion. About 1 in 5 are silent (same page); eligible_pct removes them

column11: Two filters. (1) Hospitalised: 6,603,709 US AMI hospitalisations over 2004 to 2014 in the National Inpatient Sample (Matetic A et al., Am J Cardiol 2020;129:10-18, doi:10.1016/j.amjcard.2020.05.025, PMID 32576369), 600,337 a year, 0.7458 of the CDC's 805,000. (2) Type 1 heart attack confirmed by invasive angiography, an ARTEMIS entry criterion (registry): coronary angiography in 63.4% of the lowest income quartile and 64.3% of the highest (same paper); the midpoint 0.6385 is used. 0.7458 x 0.6385 = 0.4762, about 383,000 patients a year
column12: Judgement on the midpoint, since the paper's abstract gives the two extreme quartiles and not the total. Two ARTEMIS criteria are not applied because no source for their share was found: symptom onset within 12 hours (STEMI) or 24 hours (NSTEMI) before admission, and at least one risk enhancer (prior heart attack, prior revascularisation, treated diabetes, CKD, prior ischaemic stroke, carotid or peripheral artery disease, multivessel disease, or an anterior STEMI). Both cut the pool, so 0.4762 is an upper bound on them. The case for lower: the sample counts admissions, so transfers are counted twice, and admissions have fallen since 2004 to 2014. The case for higher: a label may read 'adults with acute MI' without the angiography condition

column10: share of each year's eligible patients
column11: Incumbent: PCSK9 antibodies, the injectable add-on used for secondary prevention after a heart attack. US starts within one year of an MI hospitalisation, July 2015 to June 2020: 0.4% in Medicare, 0.4% in Optum CDM and 0.7% in MarketScan (Sloot R et al., Epidemiology 2024;35(4):579-588, doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000001730, PMID 38629975). Weighted by the NSTEMI payer mix (Medicare 62.9%, the rest 37.1% at MarketScan's commercial 0.7%; Vallabhajosyula 2021): 0.5113%. Scaled to 2025 by the class's Medicare Part D beneficiaries: Repatha's three presentations 111,259 plus Praluent Pen 52,834 = 164,093 in 2020 (drug_demand), and 609,044 plus 84,102 = 693,146 in 2025 (quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), 4.2241 times. 0.5113% x 4.2241 = 2.16%
column12: Judgement: a multiple of 1.0 on the updated PCSK9 rate. Scaling by beneficiaries treats growth in the class's Medicare stock as growth in post-heart-attack starts; with about half stopping each year the stock settles in two to three years, so its growth mostly reflects starts. 2024 and 2025 include the Part D redesign, which is permanent and applies to a 2029 launch too. Optum CDM mixes commercial and Medicare Advantage, so MarketScan is taken as the commercial rate; at the CDM and MarketScan average the anchor is 0.4557% and the peak 1.93%. No independent forecast covers this indication: GlobalData's $148mm US by 2038 (pharmaceutical-technology.com, December 2024) predates ZEUS and covers CKD, ASCVD and heart failure, and the $3bn consensus quoted before ZEUS is withdrawn by the trial's failure. The case for higher: the drug would be started in hospital at the index event with no LDL threshold to meet. The case for lower: ZEUS showed no MACE benefit despite full IL-6 suppression, so cardiologists may doubt an anti-inflammatory even after a positive ARTEMIS, and payers will meet a biologic in an 800,000-a-year population with the restrictions they put on PCSK9s

column11: the book's cardiovascular prevention curve, carried by the olpasiran, lepodisiran and AZD0780 seeds: Leqvio's CMS Part D beneficiaries went 721 in 2022 to 2,681 in 2024 (drug_demand), ln(2,681 / 721) / 2 = 0.657
column12: Reused so one class of launch keeps one curve. It is fitted to a beneficiary count, which is a treated stock; with about half of patients stopping each year the stock here follows starts within about a year, so the gap is smaller than for Leqvio itself. The case against: an in-hospital start written into post-heart-attack order sets could ramp faster than an outpatient lipid injectable once guidelines adopt it
